text:
vikram: Heads-up — noticed a mismatch between the entitlement matrix API and the console preview. When I create a route-level quota override via the API the console shows the route as ALLOWED but runtime is rejecting calls with 403 quota. Anyone else hit this?
jamie: hmm, can you paste the API body you used?
vikram: sure — small snippet: ```PATCH /v1/tenants/t-123/entitlements/{id}
{
  "principal": "team:payment-service",
  "scopeExpression": "route:/inference/* and env:prod",
  "quota": { "tokens_per_minute": 1200 }
}```
ellie: quick Q — console still renders based on the legacy `scopes` field, not `scopeExpression`. We rolled `scopeExpression` in the API last week for richer boolean logic but didn't wire the preview renderer. That would explain the visual mismatch.
vikram: ahhhh. runtime uses the compiled scopeExpression so it's correctly blocking. Console is lying to users. Not great.
kevin: high priority. If console doesn't reflect real enforcement people will think runtime is buggy. Two questions: 1) do we break any existing tenants if we change the preview? 2) what's the minimal fix for the rollout?
jamie: for 1) no — the API still accepts `scopes` and `scopeExpression`. We added `scopeExpression` as optional. But the preview logic needs to parse/compile the expression to the same normalized AST the runtime uses.
ellie: minimal path — call the internal entitlement-compiler service from the console to get a canonical preview response. That service already exists (used by runtime) and returns an AST + human-readable summary. Would need auth and a thin shim in the console backend.
vikram: sounds reasonable. Any telemetry gaps if console starts calling compiler? We want to track preview anomalies (when UI allowed != runtime allowed).
console-bot: Deploy notifier: new entitlement-compiler v2 deployed to staging at 3411112300 :rocket:
kevin: dig into telemetry — we should emit a "preview_consistency" event in the compiler: {ui_result, runtime_result, tenant, author}. Then console can surface a warning banner for mismatches and we can backfill a dashboard.
ellie: agreed. Also recommend we implement a short-lived canary: enable the compiler-based preview for 10% of orgs (config flag) with an opt-out toggle in org settings. Roll out over 48h and monitor error rates + false positives.
jamie: developer handoff: I'll add an endpoint to console-backend /internal/compile-preview that proxies to entitlement-compiler. It will return `{compiled_expression, ui_summary, allowed_routes}`. Keep response small.
vikram: for UX — please add an inline help pill: "Preview is generated from the live policy compiler; if this differs from runtime enforcement, please file a ticket." We should avoid scaring customers but be transparent.
kevin: on the telemetry dashboard: create a time series of mismatch rate per tenant, and a top-10 list of failing scopeExpression patterns. Also add alert: > 0.5% mismatch across production-tenants sustained for 30m.
jamie: one implementation note — compiler currently mutates global config for feature flags; we must ensure console proxy uses a read-only compile path. I'll add a readOnly flag to the compile API.
ellie: noted. Also check auth: console-backend will need service token with limited scope (compiler:compile:preview). Security will audit.
vikram: OK next steps: jamie to open PR with proxy + readOnly compile, ellie to run canary plan, kevin to add telemetry events + dashboard tile, and I'll draft comms for customers if we need to backfill corrections.
jamie: starting PR now, will tag reviewers.
vikram: thanks — can we target canary tomorrow morning?
ellie: yes, staging validated by EOD.
kevin: putting a placeholder on dashboards for tom.
vikram: sweet. If anyone sees other weirdness in entitlement APIs drop it here. :thumbsup:
